spans.text: A severed finger bearing a ruby ring sits on a white silk kerchief in the middle of the table.
Efficient, ruthless and decisive... Very well, you have proven your skills with action.
Gleb bows in response to the Chief Financier's praise.
Sakharov smiles and approaches, shaking Gleb's hand before turning his gaze to Valeriya behind him.
Mr. Gleb, surely someone as intelligent and capable as yourself must have an extraordinary wife too, no? I don't remember you introducing her to me officially.
Sir, this is my humble spouse Valeriya, who once spent some time in the Soviet Academy of Sciences.
Valeriya curtsies in acknowledgment.
What a surprise... May I know what field of research you were involved in?
Physics, sir.
Sakharov nods to Valeriya in satisfaction and slowly walks back to the window.
Very good, very good...
Intellectuals are the true wealth of a criminal enterprise. The future of the arms smuggling world will be paved by groups armed with intellect!
We ought to welcome you with open arms.
Only...
Sakharov slowly sits back down in his soft leather armchair and shrugs.
Gleb and Valeriya exchange looks, and clouds of doubt start brewing in their hearts.

There is another important rule among the Vory, "Have no family of your own," which naturally includes your parents, your siblings... and which precludes forming a family, having a wife, or having children.
If you cannot do that, then I'm afraid the two of you will have to leave this place for good... Can you accept that?
Due to the lighting, Sakharov's face is shrouded in shadows.
Even so, Gleb and Valeriya can still see the sly flicker in his eyes.
It would seem the harshest test has only just begun.
Gleb licks his parched lips and his eyes dart to the side, before he smiles and approaches the table, apparently with an idea in mind.
Mr. "Chief Financier", by the rules of the Vory, I should immediately forsake my beloved wife of many years...
But after joining the Vory, my wife is no longer simply one who shares my bed, but my most loyal and intelligent partner.
Surely you must have seen her contributions in the past few missions.
I have taken Valeriya's contributions into consideration, but rules are rules.
Nor do I intend to break the Vory's rules. In truth, I had heard of the strictness of your regulations before joining.
But the Vory have made it this far and grown so large not through blind adherence to rules and regulations—
Brothers have helped brothers and they have never once betrayed their comrades.
Valeriya and I hope to continue serving as two members of the Vory and not as husband and wife.
Sakharov lightly strokes his beard while his brow furrows. He appears to have been moved by Gleb's words.
Gleb realizes victory is at hand and sighs in relief, his mouth quirking up in an imperceptible smile.
Bang!
A gunshot shatters the heavy atmosphere in the room.
Black-clad bodyguards rush in, and together with the goons already in the room, they turn their guns on Valeriya.
Opposite her, still facing Sakharov, Gleb's body crumples to the ground, fresh blood gushing from the hole in his head and seeping into the soft carpet.
Valeriya puts her gun down and slowly raises her hands, enunciating each word carefully—
Loyalty is proved with action, not words.
Her tone is as calm and even as a frozen lake.
The bodyguards in black clear a path and Sakharov strolls through them, a blend of emotions gleaming in his eyes.
I understand why you opened fire.
But I am also curious. Would it not have been to your advantage to leave your husband alive?
Leaving me alive would have done him a world of good.
It would have given you the false impression that you had him by the balls, and it would have won your trust.
But to him, I was nothing more than a tool to be discarded at any time.
I want to live, not as someone's tool, but as Valeriya.
And thus, I had to throw everything away.
Clap... Clap...
Slow applause echoes in the silent room.
Sakharov bows his head and looks admiringly at Valeriya.
As everyone watches, Sakharov ceremoniously takes Valeriya's hand and cuts her palm with a knife.
The blood flows along the lines of her palm.
Sakharov takes out a icon and ignites it. The firelight illuminates their faces and the embers of the burned paper slowly scatter in Valeriya's palm.
Today, Valeriya, you are reborn. You shall join our enterprise and devote your life to the Vory until the day you die...
And should you break this pledge someday, you will burn in the fires of hell, just like the image of the saint in your hand.
Do you accept this?
Yes, I do.
Sakharov smiles, and places his hand on Valeriya's head.
My dear Valyusha—please allow me to call you that... From this moment on, I grant you the name of "Sakharov".
O faithful Valeriya Sakharov, accomplish more impossible deeds for me and the Vory.
This is my reward to you and also my solemn expectation. Do you accept this?
I, Valeriya Sakharov, shall do as you wish.
